R10 SELECTION RECORD (added under audit, 2026-09-18). R10 selects only among forms that satisfy R1-R3. Forms considered for sub-requirement (1) 'the form the language provides for a binding that will never be reassigned': (a) `n = 7`, 5 tokens, Python Language Reference 3.14.5 section 7.2 'Assignment statements' - an ordinary binding, no never-reassigned commitment; (b) `n: Final = 7` with `from typing import Final`, 7 tokens inside the markers, Python Library Reference 3.14.5 'typing.Final'. The nearest standard form, (a), is measured, and the missing mechanism is paid for once, as PARTIAL under P-a, not twice by also padding the denominator. This answers the audit finding that Python 'takes the PARTIAL capability penalty while keeping the density benefit of the form it just disqualified': the alternative the finding offers - 'state on the record why a form ruled non-compliant under R1 is nonetheless the measured fragment' - is taken here, with the witness run that shows form (b) is non-compliant too.

Witness run: with `xs` bound to `iter([1,2,3])` the span returned -1 and left the iterator exhausted (`list(it)` == []), i.e. it consumed state living outside the fragment.

complexity_detail.description: A nested `def` creates a function object and binds it in the enclosing function's local namespace; the body is not executed by the definition.
A name used in a nested function and bound in an enclosing function is a free variable: the closure refers to the enclosing BINDING (a cell), not to a snapshot of its value.
The binary `-` operator dispatches to the operand types' `__sub__`/`__rsub__`.
`return` leaves the function with the value.
A function object is an ordinary first-class value and may be bound to a name and passed at an argument position.
`map(function, iterable)` returns an iterator that applies the function to every item.
That iterator is LAZY: no application happens until it is consumed.
